title: Verifier-Guided Bounded Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study under Shared Initial Candidate Semantics
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) on identical single-shot initial generations for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran N = 200 preregistered tasks with the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling). Deterministic reconciliation reports 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Baseline configurations passed the deterministic verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact-binomial convention); paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single observed improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence ordering violation in an extreme multi-step task. We report preregistration, deterministic task and verifier design, complete execution accounting (timestamps and provider-call audit), paired confirmatory analysis, representative difficulty diagnostics, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Translating high-level human intent into device configurations is a promising application of large language models (LLMs) for network operations (NetOps). Real deployments require generated artifacts to satisfy deterministic invariants—ordering constraints, allowed-field restrictions, group-availability policies, and syntactic/semantic rules—because violations can produce transient outages or unsafe rollouts. A common architectural pattern is generate→validate→repair (guarded pipelines) where a verifier rejects unsafe candidates and triggers bounded repair. Empirically quantifying the marginal value of verifier-triggered repairs is essential for system designers deciding whether to accept automated corrections and how to allocate verification budget.

A subtle but important methodological choice affects interpretation: when paired comparisons reuse the very same generated candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), any observed paired difference can only be caused by downstream validator-triggered repair rather than generator-side factors (prompting, sampling variability, or multi-sample selection). We preregistered and executed CAND-2026-001 to estimate precisely this repair-only estimand: the per-task paired difference in binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier when baseline and guarded episodes begin from the identical single initial generation and guarded logic is permitted at most one automated repair. The paired shared-initial design isolates whether a bounded verifier-triggered repair can convert otherwise failing single-shot candidate outputs into verifier-passing configurations.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and engineering work on LLM-driven NetOps has produced prototype generators, benchmarks, and surveys that document the feasibility of intent→configuration synthesis and the need for operationally meaningful evaluation [NetConfEval et al.; other intent→config prototypes]. Deterministic verifiers have been developed in networking research to check syntactic invariants and workflow-ordering constraints; they provide an oracle appropriate for configuration correctness assessments [Beckett et al.].

Across adjacent technical domains, generate→validate→repair pipelines are an established pattern: program-repair systems show that executable tests can drive corrective patches [Li 2024; Copiloting the Copilots], and agentic tool-augmented frameworks couple models to external solvers or validators to increase reliability [Dong 2026; surveys of agentic AI]. These works motivate guarded designs in NetOps, but the literature supplied with this study generally demonstrates proposals, demonstrations, or domain-adjacent empirical results rather than definitive multi-environment production claims. Tool-augmented agent literature also highlights engineering challenges for safe validator coupling: oracle specification, provenance, and auditable protocols are necessary to reason about operational correctness [TRIPOD-LLM; Dong 2026].

Synthesis. The supplied literature establishes that (i) intent→config pipelines and benchmark-style evaluations are active research directions; (ii) deterministic verifiers are a natural operational oracle to test many operational invariants; and (iii) generate→validate→repair is a promising architectural pattern demonstrated in adjacent domains but requires domain-specific, verifier-integrated empirical evaluation to quantify repair-only effects under paired, shared-candidate semantics. Our experiment addresses the empirical gap of measuring the marginal repair effect when identical initial candidates are reused across baseline and guarded conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 before any model calls. The primary confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: per-task difference in binary "all-specified-invariants-pass" rates between guarded and baseline, paired by task. Preregistration fixed task_count = 200, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both conditions), maximum one automated repair call per task, and the primary confirmatory test = exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial-tail convention). The preregistration and execution manifest are archived in the execution bundle.

Deterministic task bank and verifier. Tasks were produced by a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with a fixed deterministic selection rule. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence ordering constraints, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields). The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated configurations, enforces allowed_fields and required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants, and returns binary full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. Validator tracer outputs are authoritative scoring evidence and are archived.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics, temperature, and sampling notes. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the same single initial generation (one sampled candidate) was provided to baseline and guarded episodes. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise from the verifier and the permitted repair; it cannot arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, different sampling calls, prompt variants, or multi-sample selection. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property even though each pair used a single sampled initial candidate by design.

Sanitizer, repair policy, and provider-call accounting. A deterministic formatting sanitizer ran before verifier parsing. If the verifier reported invariant violations, guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model with a repair prompt constructed from the verifier tracer (preregistered). Deterministic reconciliation records authoritative stage-level provider counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, summing to hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0 indicate fresh provider calls for every stage invocation. All provider-call accounting and stage counts are archived.

Confirmatory statistical procedures. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01 using the exact binomial-tail convention implemented in the archived analysis executor. Paired absolute risk difference uses a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples and seed 1729 (parameters recorded in the analysis log). Primary failed-call treatment followed preregistration (complete_pair_primary); sensitivity analyses treating persistent unparsables as failures are preregistered but not needed here because no persistent unparsables occurred.
sections.results:
Execution and audit. The run executed in execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory and completed both episodes for all 200 preregistered tasks (planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0). The run timestamps record start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (elapsed ≈29 minutes). Deterministic reconciliation reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and cache_miss_count = 201, matching preregistration expectations for shared_initial_candidate semantics and a single repair invocation across all pairs.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic verifier judged baseline successes = 199 and failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995) and guarded successes = 200 and failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, yielding paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With total discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the archived exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial-tail convention) is p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric results are reproduced by the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor when run on the recorded raw results.

Single repair event and diagnostic trace. Exactly one automated repair occurred. Archived verifier traces for the repaired pair document that the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint; the preregistered bounded repair policy produced a corrected command ordering and the verifier trace records validation_after.valid = true with repair_applied = true. Difficulty metadata associated with the repaired episode indicate an extreme composite pattern (required_command_count up to 9; changed_interface_count up to 3; difficulty.level = "extreme"). Representative tasks in the archive show required_command_count spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count reaching 3; the single baseline failure (and the repaired episode) are associated with an extreme multi-step ordering pattern.

Missingness, exclusions, and consistency checks. No preregistered exclusions or persistent unparsables were recorded. The analysis missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros in all other missingness categories. Deterministic reconciliation reports pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. Provider-call audits align with the preregistered execution contract.
sections.discussion:
What we measured and what the estimand means. Because the study enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics, both baseline and guarded conditions began from the exact same sampled candidate for each task. Consequently the confirmatory estimand isolates the marginal downstream effect of the deterministic verifier plus at-most-one bounded repair on an already-sampled single-shot candidate: baseline single-shot/initial validity versus final guarded-pipeline validity after deterministic validation and permitted repair. Under this estimand the observed paired difference (one repaired success) is direct evidence that a bounded verifier-triggered repair can convert at least some verifier-detectable ordering violations into verifier-passing configurations.

Discordant-pair structure, ceiling effects, and inferential scope. The observed contingency counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) place the experiment in a sparse-discordant regime. With only one discordant pair the exact McNemar p-value provides limited directional inferential power (p = 1.0 under the exact-binomial-tail convention), while the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] bounds the plausible absolute improvement attributable to repair under the repair-only estimand and the specific resampling scheme (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered power rationale—targeting detection of ~10–15 percentage-point paired increases at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions—was predicated on a substantially lower baseline success rate than observed. The realized baseline success rate (99.5%) therefore created a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to small repair-only effects; this is an important operational observation rather than a procedural failure.

Observed failure-mode concentration. Archived tracer fields and difficulty metadata show verifier-detectable residual failures concentrate on complex multi-device workflows that impose strict required_sequence ordering constraints and multiple dependent field changes. Representative archived tasks with extreme difficulty patterns (required_command_count = 9; changed_interface_count = 3) exhibited higher fragility under single-shot generation than simpler tasks. The single repaired episode involved correcting a required-sequence ordering breach; the archived repair prompt and post-repair validation trace document the repair logic and its corrective effect. These grounded observations support an exploratory hypothesis—consistent with prior program-repair and synthesis literature—that when initial generation quality is high, residual verifier-detectable faults are dominated by ordering/dependency composition rather than isolated per-device syntax issues.

Operational implications (bounded). Artifact-grounded evidence supports this constrained operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank evaluated with the declared hosted model gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-guided bounded repair can correct certain ordering/dependency violations in verifier-expressible tasks. However, because the study measured a repair-only estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics, these results are not evidence that guarded prompting, multi-sample selection, independent guarded first-pass generation, or multi-model strategies would yield similar or larger gains. Likewise, passing the deterministic verifier is necessary for the encoded invariants but not sufficient to guarantee safe production deployment across heterogeneous vendors and live dataplanes; live-device emulation and vendor-runtime testing remain necessary external validation steps.

Design guidance for system builders. When single-shot generation quality is already high, bounded verifier-triggered repair under a shared-initial regimen yields at most small marginal gains in per-task verifier acceptance in this synthetic verifier-backed setting; nonetheless, the repair mechanism demonstrably corrected an extreme sequencing violation when present. Designers should therefore weigh where verification invariants expose correctable ordering or dependency faults and whether permitting bounded automated repairs is acceptable for their operational risk profile. If sampling variability or prompt engineering account for most failures in a target environment, experiments that allow independent guarded first-pass generations or multi-sample selection are required to measure generator-side mitigation effects; those contrasts were intentionally out of scope here because of the preregistered shared_initial_candidate estimand.

Threats to validity and reproducibility notes. Internal validity benefits from deterministic task selection, archived verifier traces, and the enforced shared_initial_candidate contract, which isolates repair-only effects. Construct validity is limited by verifier expressiveness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces encoded invariants but does not execute commands on real devices and therefore cannot observe runtime-only behaviors or vendor idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank focused on very_hard and extreme patterns; generalization requires multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded arms, and live-device or dataplane emulation. All execution artifacts, provider-call accounting, and analysis logs are archived to support reanalysis.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired study that conservatively measured the marginal effect of allowing one verifier-triggered bounded repair on identical single-shot LLM-generated network-configuration candidates. Across 200 deterministic synthetic tasks evaluated with a deterministic verifier and the declared hosted model gpt-5-mini (temperature recorded as null/unset), baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; one automated repair corrected an extreme ordering violation. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. These artifact-grounded results support a narrowly scoped practical inference: bounded verifier-triggered repair can correct localized ordering faults expressible by the verifier in synthetic tasks when initial single-shot generation quality is already high. Broader claims about multi-model benefits, independent guarded-generation effects, adversarial robustness, or dataplane correctness remain open empirical questions requiring additional, distinct experiments. The preregistration, execution manifest, verifier traces, provider-call audit, and analysis artifacts are archived to enable reanalysis and controlled extensions of this work.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.

Ceiling-effect sensitivity: the realized baseline success rate (99.5%) substantially reduced the study's sensitivity to detect small repair-only improvements compared with preregistered mid-range baseline assumptions.
